topic: Segmentation and quantification of vessels, airway and bone in the neck (Margin / hnrad, local-only CPU)

findings.title: TotalSegmentator (wasserth/TotalSegmentator) - 100+ CT/MR structures incl. common carotid arteries, internal jugular veins, trachea, mandible, skull
findings.summary: nnU-Net based pip package. The 'total' task covers trachea, skull, mandible-adjacent bone; the 'headneck_bones_vessels' and 'aortic_branches'/'heartchambers' subtasks add common carotid arteries, brachiocephalic trunk, subclavian and internal jugular veins. Reported Dice ~0.90 overall on its own test set.
findings.relevance: Single best first-pass backbone for Margin: gives carotid, IJV, trachea, mandible, skull masks in one run so the viewer can overlay vessels/airway/bone without training anything.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 code; model weights free for non-commercial/academic use, some subtasks require a license key from the author
findings.feasibility: pip installable, pure PyTorch CPU path works (--fast --device cpu); expect minutes per volume on Intel iGPU box. torch CPU wheels cover Python 3.9-3.14 on Windows, so 3.13 is fine; the residual risk is nnunetv2's own pinned deps, not torch.

findings.title: Automatic Segmentation of Cardiovascular Structures on Chest CT Data Sets: An Update of the TotalSegmentator
findings.summary: De-novo annotation and model update adding supra-aortic vessels that TotalSegmentator previously lacked: brachiocephalic trunk, bilateral common carotid arteries, brachiocephalic veins, superior vena cava. Reports per-structure Dice on chest CT.
findings.relevance: Documents exactly which carotid/venous classes exist and how they were validated - the citation Margin needs when displaying a carotid label and its expected accuracy.
findings.feasibility: Reference only. Note: validation is chest CT, so cervical ICA above the bifurcation is out of the validated range - Margin must caveat this.

findings.title: Value of MR and CT Imaging for Assessment of Internal Carotid Artery Encasement in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
findings.summary: Systematic assessment of ICA encasement on MR/CT. The >270 degrees circumferential-contact threshold predicts unresectability; <=270 degrees interpreted as lack of invasion. Encasement missed in only ~1.5% of operable-selection cases, but inter-observer variation limits reliability.
findings.relevance: The literature anchor for Margin's carotid encasement readout: compute degrees of tumour-vessel circumferential contact per axial slice and flag >270 deg. Also justifies showing observer-variability caveats.
findings.feasibility: Pure geometry on existing masks: per-slice polar sweep from vessel centroid, count arc where tumour mask is within a tolerance of the vessel boundary. Trivially CPU, numpy only.

findings.title: Prediction model based on preoperative CT findings for carotid artery invasion in patients with head and neck masses
findings.summary: CT-based multivariable model. Beyond the 270-degree rule, encasement angle, tumour-artery contact length (<=26 mm cut-point), arterial deformation, tortuosity, stenosis and loss of the intervening fat plane predicted true arterial wall invasion.
findings.relevance: Extends Margin's carotid module past a single angle: also report contact LENGTH in mm along the vessel centreline, vessel deformation (eccentricity) and fat-plane obliteration - all derivable from the same masks.
findings.feasibility: All metrics computable from binary masks + HU sampling in the perivascular ring. numpy/SimpleITK, CPU, milliseconds.

findings.title: Resectability Issues with Head and Neck Cancer (AJNR)
findings.summary: Radiology review defining imaging criteria for unresectability in head and neck cancer, including carotid encasement thresholds, prevertebral/retropharyngeal involvement, skull base and mediastinal extension.
findings.relevance: Source for Margin's overall 'resectability checklist' panel - tells the app which structures to quantify and what thresholds to surface alongside the carotid angle.
findings.feasibility: Reference only.

findings.title: ToothFairy / ToothFairy2 / ToothFairy3 - Inferior Alveolar Canal and multi-structure CBCT segmentation challenges
findings.summary: ToothFairy (2023) released 443 CBCT scans with 153 voxel-level IAC annotations - largest public IAC dataset. ToothFairy2 (2024) added mandible, teeth, maxilla and pharynx; ToothFairy3 (2025) expands to 77 classes plus a runtime-aware track and an interactive IAC track.
findings.relevance: Source of pretrained-model recipes and ground truth for Margin's mandibular canal overlay during mandibulectomy / marginal-vs-segmental planning. The runtime-aware track is directly relevant to CPU inference budgets.
findings.license: challenge data under CC-BY-NC style terms - check per-edition data use agreement
findings.feasibility: Data is CBCT, not contrast neck CT; models are nnU-Net based so CPU inference is feasible but slow. Registration required to download.

findings.title: DentalSegmentator - open source nnU-Net for CT and CBCT: maxilla/upper skull, mandible, upper teeth, lower teeth, mandibular canal
findings.venue_or_repo: Journal of Dentistry; 3D Slicer extension; weights on Zenodo
findings.summary: Trained on 470 dento-maxillo-facial CT/CBCT scans, tested on 256 scans from 7 institutions. Mean Dice 92.2 +/- 6.3% internal (n=133) and 94.2 +/- 7.4% external (n=123). Ships as a one-click 3D Slicer extension with public pretrained weights.
findings.relevance: Best single source for Margin's mandible + inferior alveolar canal + tooth masks on ordinary neck CT (it is explicitly trained on CT, not just CBCT). Weights can be called directly from nnUNetv2 in our FastAPI backend without Slicer.
findings.license: open source (Apache-2.0 style); weights published on Zenodo
findings.feasibility: nnU-Net v2 CPU inference; a head CT at 0.5-1 mm will be slow but tractable in 32 GB. Downloadable as a static Zenodo archive, which suits a proxied network.

findings.title: DentalSegmentator pretrained nnU-Net weights (Zenodo record 10829675)
findings.summary: Direct download of the DentalSegmentator nnU-Net checkpoint used by the 3D Slicer extension, with the 5-class label map (maxilla/upper skull, mandible, upper teeth, lower teeth, mandibular canal).
findings.relevance: The concrete artefact Margin would vendor locally so bone/teeth/canal inference runs entirely offline.
findings.feasibility: Single archive, no runtime network access needed after download - exactly what a local-only, proxied, no-admin install requires.

findings.title: Quantitative assessment of the upper airway in infants and children with subglottic stenosis
findings.summary: Defines PR(ASG): percent reduction of subglottic cross-sectional area relative to a predicted healthy subglottis derived from the patient's own mid-trachea area. Cross-sectional areas computed at subglottis (ASG) and mid-trachea (AMT) from segmented CT airway.
findings.relevance: Gives Margin a self-normalising stenosis metric that does not need age-matched norms: report minimal CSA, mid-trachea CSA, and percent reduction, then map onto Myer-Cotton bands.
findings.feasibility: Requires an airway mask plus centreline-perpendicular resampling. All doable in SimpleITK/numpy on CPU.

findings.title: VMTK - the Vascular Modeling Toolkit (centreline extraction, cross-sectional area, tube geometry)
findings.summary: Reference implementation for centreline extraction (vmtkcenterlines), maximum-inscribed-sphere radius, branch splitting and perpendicular cross-sectional area - used for both vessels and airway lumen. Also exposed as the 3D Slicer 'Extract Centerline' module.
findings.relevance: Would provide Margin's airway centreline + minimal CSA and the carotid centreline for contact-length measurement.
findings.feasibility: WARNING: pip distribution is frozen at VMTK 1.3; 1.4+ is conda-only and needs compiled VTK/ITK. On Python 3.13 with no admin and a proxy this is a real risk. Practical fallback: use vtk (pip wheel, BSD) + skimage.morphology.skeletonize_3d + scipy distance transform to roll our own centreline and CSA.

findings.title: AutoSeg4ETICA - nnU-Net framework for Eustachian tube and INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY segmentation with automatic ET-ICA distance computation
findings.summary: nnU-Net trained on 30 CT scans (60 ET/ICA pairs). ICA Dice 0.884 with average Hausdorff distance 0.246 mm; ET Dice 0.578. Repo includes preprocessing, training, inference and evaluation code, and computes structure-to-structure distances.
findings.relevance: The closest existing work to Margin's carotid module: a skull-base ICA segmenter PLUS an automated distance-to-adjacent-structure readout - exactly the pattern needed for carotid-to-pharyngeal-wall and carotid-to-tumour distances.
findings.feasibility: PyTorch/nnU-Net, CPU inference workable on a single head CT. Small training set (n=30) so expect domain shift on our contrast neck CTs - use as a fine-tuning starting point, not a drop-in.

findings.title: The Retropharyngeal Internal Carotid Artery: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis of the Current Literature, and Evidence Sampling
findings.summary: PRISMA systematic review and first pooled prevalence estimate for retropharyngeal ICA (RP-ICA), a cervical ICA variant coursing adjacent to or abutting the pharyngeal wall and reducing the safety margin for nasotracheal intubation and transoral surgery.
findings.relevance: The evidence base for a Margin safety flag: measure minimum 3D distance from the ICA mask to the posterior pharyngeal mucosal surface and warn before transoral / TORS / tonsil-bed procedures.
findings.feasibility: Reference only; the metric itself is a distance transform between two masks - SimpleITK SignedMaurerDistanceMap, CPU, sub-second.

findings.title: Clinically significant anatomical variation of the retropharyngeal internal carotid arteries
findings.summary: Imaging series characterising clinically significant RP-ICA. Reported minimum ICA-to-pharyngeal-wall distances in high-risk cases around 3.3-4.9 mm, down to direct contact with the posterior pharyngeal wall.
findings.relevance: Supplies the concrete millimetre thresholds Margin should use to colour-code its carotid-to-pharyngeal-wall distance readout (e.g. <5 mm = high risk, contact = critical).
findings.feasibility: Reference only.

findings.title: HaN-Seg: head and neck organ-at-risk CT & MR segmentation dataset (42 patients, 30 OARs including A_Carotid_L/R and Bone_Mandible)
findings.venue_or_repo: Zenodo / Medical Physics (Podobnik et al., doi 10.1002/mp.16197)
findings.summary: 42 patients with paired CT and T1 MR for IGRT, with curated expert binary masks for 30 OARs named per AAPM TG-263, explicitly including left/right carotid arteries and the mandible on head and neck CT.
findings.relevance: The single best public ground truth for validating (or fine-tuning) Margin's carotid and mandible masks on genuine head and neck CT geometry rather than chest or dental CBCT.
findings.license: public on Zenodo; citation of the Medical Physics paper required - verify the CC terms on the record before redistribution
findings.feasibility: Plain NRRD/NIfTI download, no runtime dependency. Usable purely as a local offline validation set - no PHI leaves the device.

findings.title: HaN-Seg 2023 challenge (organ-at-risk CT/MR segmentation challenge results)
findings.summary: Challenge paper reporting per-OAR Dice and 95% Hausdorff for competing methods across the 30 head and neck OARs, giving realistic accuracy expectations for small tubular structures such as the carotid arteries versus large ones such as the mandible.
findings.relevance: Benchmark numbers Margin can quote when reporting carotid/mandible segmentation confidence, and a shortlist of architectures worth reusing.
findings.feasibility: Reference only.

findings.title: SlicerExtension-VMTK - Extract Centerline and Cross-Section Analysis modules
findings.summary: Brings VMTK into 3D Slicer. 'Extract Centerline' handles vessel, airway or any tree structure and is faster and more robust than raw VMTK; 'Cross-Section Analysis' measures cross-sectional area, diameter and derived metrics perpendicular to the centreline and outputs tables and plots. Fully scriptable from Python.
findings.relevance: Direct blueprint for Margin's airway stenosis readout (CSA vs arc length, nadir CSA) and carotid contact-length measurement. The module source is readable Python we can port into the FastAPI backend without shipping Slicer.
findings.feasibility: Best path for Margin: port the algorithm (VTK-based, no compiled VMTK required for the centreline curve + cross-section area math) rather than depending on conda-only VMTK 1.4. vtk ships Windows wheels on PyPI, user-level installable.

findings.title: ATM'22 - Multi-site, Multi-domain Airway Tree Modeling benchmark (500 annotated CT airway trees)
findings.venue_or_repo: Grand Challenge / Medical Image Analysis 2023; code collection at github.com/EndoluminalSurgicalVision-IMR/ATM-22-Related-Work
findings.summary: 500 chest CTs with full airway-tree annotations (300 train / 50 val / 150 test) plus task-tailored metrics (branch and tree detected rate). Top-10 methods used nnU-Net, 3D U-Net, WingsNet and Attention U-Net variants.
findings.relevance: Source of pretrained airway models and loss functions for Margin's tracheal/laryngeal lumen segmentation. Only the proximal airway (trachea, subglottis) matters for us, which is the easiest part of the task - so off-the-shelf models should transfer well.
findings.license: challenge data agreement (research use); linked code repos vary, mostly MIT/Apache
findings.feasibility: Full bronchial-tree models are heavy; for trachea-only we can crop to the neck and run at coarse spacing, which is very CPU-friendly.

findings.title: NaviAirway - bronchiole-sensitive deep learning airway segmentation pipeline
findings.summary: Airway segmentation pipeline using a bronchiole-sensitive loss and a human-vision-inspired iterative training strategy to recover fine distal branches; ships inference scripts and pretrained weights.
findings.relevance: Alternative airway backbone if TotalSegmentator's trachea class is too coarse at the subglottis. Its thin-structure loss is also applicable to the inferior alveolar canal.
findings.license: check repository LICENSE before adoption (not confirmed in this pass)
findings.feasibility: PyTorch, sliding-window 3D inference - slow on CPU for whole chest, acceptable for a cropped neck volume.

findings.title: AeroPath: an airway segmentation benchmark dataset with challenging pathology
findings.summary: Public airway CT dataset deliberately enriched for pathology (stenosis, tumour compression, distorted anatomy) rather than normal anatomy, with an accompanying open pipeline and demo.
findings.relevance: Critically relevant: Margin's airway cases ARE the pathological ones (tumour-narrowed larynx/trachea). Standard airway models trained on normals degrade exactly here, and AeroPath is the honest test set.
findings.license: open (MIT-style for code; data openly released - verify on the repo)
findings.feasibility: Data + lightweight models; the authors provide CPU-runnable demo inference.

findings.title: Occlusion of the internal jugular vein in differentiated thyroid carcinoma: causes and diagnosis
findings.summary: Separates four mechanisms of IJV occlusion on contrast CT: bland thrombus, tumour thrombus, extrinsic compression or direct invasion by tumour/nodes, and post-dissection fibrotic collapse. Notes CT signs of tumour thrombus (similar attenuation to tumour, irregular luminal expansion, post-contrast thrombus enhancement).
findings.relevance: Defines what Margin's IJV panel should report: patency, cross-sectional area versus contralateral side, intraluminal filling defect, and whether the defect enhances - each computable from the IJV mask plus HU statistics.
findings.feasibility: Metrics are mask statistics + HU sampling; numpy/SimpleITK, CPU, trivial.

findings.title: PAN-VIQ: a clinically validated 3D deep learning approach for quantifying vascular invasion in pancreatic cancer
findings.summary: Automated framework segmenting tumour plus five critical vessels from contrast CT and quantifying involvement via 3D ENCASEMENT ANGLES. Trained/internally validated on 2130 cases and prospectively tested in 202 patients against radiologist resectability calls.
findings.relevance: The strongest methodological template for Margin's carotid encasement module - same clinical logic (degrees of circumferential tumour contact drives resectability), same pipeline (multi-organ segmentation then geometric angle extraction), already shown to survive prospective validation in another anatomy.
findings.license: open access article; code availability to be confirmed on the paper's data/code statement
findings.feasibility: The angle computation itself is pure geometry on masks and runs in milliseconds on CPU - only the segmentation stage is expensive. Directly portable to carotid vs neck tumour.

findings.title: ToothFairy2 challenge: multi-structure CBCT segmentation (530 volumes, 42 classes, FDI-numbered teeth)
findings.summary: 530 CBCT volumes with expert 3D annotations of 42 classes: individual teeth numbered per the FDI system, mandible, maxilla, inferior alveolar canal, pharynx and related structures. Challenge paper reports per-class Dice for the leading nnU-Net based entries.
findings.relevance: Gives Margin per-tooth labelling (needed to report which teeth sit in a planned mandibulectomy segment) and a pharynx class usable alongside the carotid mask for retropharyngeal-carotid distance.
findings.feasibility: nnU-Net inference. CBCT domain - expect degradation on contrast neck CT; DentalSegmentator is the better CT-domain choice, this is better for per-tooth granularity.

findings.title: OraSeg - open deep learning framework and model for tooth instance segmentation in dental CBCT
findings.summary: Standardised annotated dataset of 35 oral anatomical structures; UNETR backbone combining Swin Transformer and a spatial Mamba module with multi-scale residual fusion. Dice 0.8316 +/- 0.0305 for CBCT tooth instance segmentation, beating SwinUNETR and 3D U-Net. Shipped as a one-click 3D Slicer tool.
findings.relevance: Per-tooth instance labels (not just a single 'teeth' class) for mandibular resection planning and dental-clearance documentation.
findings.license: free for NON-COMMERCIAL use only - acceptable for Margin as a personal clinical-research tool, blocks any future commercial path
findings.feasibility: Transformer/Mamba backbone is heavier than plain nnU-Net; Mamba kernels often assume CUDA. Verify a pure-CPU PyTorch fallback exists before adopting.

findings.title: torch on PyPI - Windows CPU wheels and Python version support matrix
findings.summary: CPU-only wheels for Windows and macOS are hosted on PyPI (GPU wheels target Linux). PyTorch currently supports Python 3.9 through 3.14 on Windows; cp313 wheels have been generally available since early 2025.
findings.relevance: Settles the core feasibility question for Margin: every nnU-Net-based model above (TotalSegmentator, DentalSegmentator, AutoSeg4ETICA) can be pip-installed at user level on Python 3.13 Windows with CPU-only torch, no admin and no CUDA.
findings.feasibility: pip install torch --index-url .../cpu works user-level behind a proxy with pip proxy settings. Set OMP_NUM_THREADS and use --fast / low-resolution nnU-Net configs to keep per-case runtime tolerable on an Intel iGPU machine.

gaps: No published model that AUTOMATES the carotid encasement angle end-to-end on head and neck CT was found - Margin would be implementing an unvalidated (if geometrically simple) derivation of a validated clinical criterion
Tooth-level (FDI-numbered) segmentation on contrast neck CT rather than CBCT remains weakly covered; dental artefact handling unaddressed
Python 3.13 wheel availability for torch / nnunetv2 / vtk on Windows not yet verified
No CPU wall-clock benchmarks for any of these models on an Intel iGPU class machine were found in the literature
